summary.problem: getRipgrepPath() never falls back to system PATH when bundled ripgrep binaries are missing.
summary.root_cause: getRipgrepPath() in packages/core/src/tools/ripGrep.ts only checks candidate vendor directory paths relative to __dirname and returns null if they do not exist.
summary.context: When @google/gemini-cli is installed globally without bundled binaries, ripgrep is reported as unavailable even if installed on system PATH.

steps: Update getRipgrepPath() in packages/core/src/tools/ripGrep.ts to check candidate vendor binary paths first.
Add fallback logic to look up system ripgrep on PATH using platform lookup ('where' on win32 or 'which' / PATH lookup on POSIX) when bundled binaries are absent.
Ensure getRipgrepPath() returns the verified path to system ripgrep or null if not found.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: getRipgrepPath() should fall back to locating system ripgrep when candidate bundled binary files do not exist.
verification_steps: Add unit tests in packages/core/src/tools/ripGrep.test.ts mocking missing bundled binary files and verifying fallback resolution to system PATH.
Run Vitest suite for packages/core/src/tools/ripGrep.test.ts to verify all tests pass.

github_metadata.title: Title: getRipgrepPath() never falls back to system PATH — ripgrep unavailable despite being installed
